title: decision-event v1
description: ONE WRITE-ONCE RECORD OF THE DECISIONS STORE: something that happened to the list of questions waiting for a person. The store is a folder, <HordeHome>\store\decisions\, holding one file per record named by its sequence number in ten digits (0000000007.json). A record is written whole and then given its name once, by a move that the operating system lets exactly one caller win, and is never rewritten or deleted (decisions/Store.ps1). The records in sequence order are the single source of truth: the current list is worked out from them each time (decisions/Rules.ps1) and nothing else is kept. ON DISK: UTF-8 with no byte-order mark, one JSON object. VERSIONING: a reader treats a record that does not match this schema as unreadable and says so by sequence number; it never guesses and never skips it silently. A record that DOES match this envelope and whose kind the reader does not know was written by a later version: it is not damage. It is set aside, reported once for its kind, and costs no question number - the compatibility contract in decisions/Rules.ps1. That contract rests on two promises: question-added is a kind every version knows, and a kind's name never changes meaning. A later kind of event is a new entry in the kind table of decisions/Rules.ps1 and a new definition here; a change to an existing kind's data, or to this envelope, is a v2.

sequence.description: The record's place in the one total order, from 1 with no gaps. It must equal the number in the record's file name.

id.description: The idempotency id the caller chose for the request that made this record: 32 lowercase hex digits. The same id with the same request is answered from this record and writes nothing; the same id with another request is refused.

kind.description: What happened. The closed list is the kind table of decisions/Rules.ps1; each kind's data is a definition below of the same name.

at.description: When the record was written, ISO 8601 in UTC with a Z, by the writer's clock. Order is the sequence, never this time.

actor.description: Who made the request, as one lowercase role label (core/roles.json names the roles). WHICH labels may write is not said here: it is the closed list of actors in decisions/Rules.ps1, asked of a request before it is written, so that a new actor is one entry there and not a new version of this schema, and so that a record written under an actor an older version does not list is still read by it.

requestHash.description: SHA-256 of the request as the rules normalised it (operation, actor and what was asked), so that a repost of an id can be told from a reuse of it without comparing whole texts.

data.description: What the kind carries, checked against the definition named for the kind.

number.description: The permanent number the question was given. It is DERIVED, not counted anywhere: the Nth question-added record is question N. It is written down here as a check on that derivation, so that a record which later becomes unreadable cannot shift the number of any question added after it.

importance.description: How much the task this question belongs to matters overall, as one lowercase label. The closed list is the importances of decisions/Rules.ps1, asked of a request; a record is read whatever label it holds. Absent - as in every record written before the word existed - reads as the default, normal.

blocks.description: How much of that task's work stands still until the question is answered, as one lowercase label. The closed list is the blockings of decisions/Rules.ps1. Absent reads as the default, part.

needsPasskey.description: The question changes something important (a production deploy), so from the phone it is answered only with a fresh passkey. Written only as true: absent - as in every record written before the mark existed, and every question that needs none - reads as no passkey needed.

followsUp.description: The number of the earlier question this one follows up on. A follow-up is a new question with a number of its own, never the earlier one opened again; the earlier question and what was answered under it are shown with this one as context, worked out from the list each time and never copied here.

changes.description: The fields that change and their new values, schema/decision-question.v1. A field not named keeps its value.

outcome.description: What was done, in plain words. Never blank.

reason.description: Why it is open again, on one line. Never blank.

question-ranked.description: The keeper corrected how much a question matters, or how much it holds up. A record of its own: the words the question was added with are never edited. It holds only what it changes; a record that names neither word changes nothing and is reported as that.

importance.description: The importance from this record on. The closed list is the importances of decisions/Rules.ps1.

blocks.description: The blocking from this record on. The closed list is the blockings of decisions/Rules.ps1.

message-said.description: Someone said something under a question. The record holds what was said and what its speaker was looking at; whether the question was closed by then, whether its wording had moved on, whose turn it now is and whether the other side has read it are DERIVED from the order of the records (decisions/Rules.ps1) and are stored nowhere.

number.description: The question the words were said under.

speaker.description: Whose words they are, as one lowercase label. The closed list is the speakers of decisions/Rules.ps1, asked of a request before it is written; it is not an enum here, so that a record written under a speaker an older version does not list is still read by it.

route.description: By what route the words arrived. The closed list is the routes of decisions/Rules.ps1. Words a person typed himself and words another hand wrote down for him are different routes, and are never stored as one.

text.description: The words, VERBATIM: never trimmed, normalised or re-wrapped, in any alphabet, with their own line breaks.

wordingVersion.description: The wording of the question the speaker was looking at (the view's wordingVersion), WHEN THE SPEAKER STATED IT. Absent means not stated: the session writing down what was said in chat does not know what was on the speaker's screen, and nothing is guessed in its place. Words are an answer to a stated wording and to no other.

asks.description: False when the keeper's words ask the founder nothing (a note): the turn does not pass to him. Absent means true.

act.description: The founder's words record an act of his: park or unpark. The turn does not pass.

evidence.description: Words answered on the founder's phone: the SHA-256, in lower-case hex, of the relay journal record that proved them. Only the hash: the envelope and its passkey signature are kept in relay's own journal (relay/Journal.ps1).

part.description: The words answer ONE PART of a question of parts: that part's letter. Each part is answered by a record of its own, and the question is the other speaker's turn once every part has one. Absent means the words are said to the whole question.

signedBy.description: Words answered on the founder's phone: the key id of the passkey the relay channel verified the answer's envelope against, written once by that channel. Absent in every record written before 2026-10-12 and for every other route: such a record names no passkey, and nothing is put in its place.

messages-read.description: A reader has read what others said, under every question, up to a record. Marking is its own record: what has been read is never a field edited on a message. A mark that moves nothing changes nothing.

reader.description: Who has read, as one lowercase label: a speaker of decisions/Rules.ps1 that has an inbox.

upTo.description: The sequence number of the last record the reader has read up to. Always below this record's own sequence number: nothing is read before it is written.

answer-routed.description: One answer of the founder's was sent, by code, to the seat of whoever asked the question - or that seat was reminded, once, that the answered question is still open (decisions/Route.ps1). One record per answer and purpose: a second does not apply, so an answer is never mailed twice. It changes nothing else of the question, and authorizes nothing.

number.description: The question the answer is under.

answer.description: The sequence number of the message-said record that holds the founder's answer.

purpose.description: answer: the answer itself was sent. nudge: the one reminder that the question is answered and still open. The closed list is decisions/Rules.ps1's.

seat.description: Whose seat it went to: orc (the Orc that asked) or warchief (the warchief asked, or askedBy could not be resolved to an Orc's seat - resolved and note say which).

label.description: The fleet label of the seat it went to (an Orc's lane letter); empty for the warchief's.

sessionId.description: The session the fleet's registry proved holds that seat when it was sent.

resolved.description: True when it went to the seat askedBy names. False when askedBy could not be resolved to a seat, and it went to the warchief instead; note says why.

notice.description: The messageId of the notice the messenger took. The same answer, purpose and seat always make the same id, so a send repeated after a crash is one message.

note.description: One line: why it did not go where askedBy names, or empty.

analyst.description: One line: what the fleet analyst was told of the answer (purpose answer), or empty.

question-acked.description: The Orc that asked a question acknowledges the founder's answer to it, and the question is closed with that Orc as the closer. Only an open question whose answer stands and is waiting for the keeper closes this way, and only for the answer that stands now; a closed question is never opened again by it (decisions/Rules.ps1).

by.description: The lane letter of the Orc that acknowledges, as its session's fleet label proves it. It must be the Orc the question's askedBy names.

answer.description: The sequence number of the founder's answer that is acknowledged: the one that stands under the question when the record is written.
